findings.message: The fix for `block_on` parsing is only partly a class fix. It handles the named case (empty list falls back to the default) and adds a 7-variant parity table. But `Config.block_on` (review_core) and `block_on()` (specclaw-sync) are still two parsers, and the table leaves out variants the previous finding listed or that are common in YAML. Missing: single-quoted items, an inline `# comment` after the value, `block_on: null` or `~`, a scalar comma list like `block_on: law, security`, and a trailing comma in a flow list. Add those rows, or make specclaw-sync call `review_core.parse_block`/`Config.block_on` so only one implementation exists.
findings.scenario: `release_gate:\n  block_on: [law] # tracked in ADR\n` or `block_on: law, security` → the two parsers can return different class lists. The sync gate then blocks a release that the review loop treated as passing, or the reverse. The parity test never exercises these inputs, so it stays green.

findings.message: The head-drift finding was handled by documenting strictness, not by changing `verdict_at`. The docs now say committing round records moves the head and no status is posted. But the same paragraph still says 'The `ci/` templates post the same status from the pipeline'. Those templates derive CHANGE from round files committed in the PR, so in that flow the head can never equal the recorded one and the status is never posted. The paragraph should say so for CI. The 'operator decision (change 064)' in the `verdict_at` docstring and SKILL.md is not recorded anywhere I can check, so cite where it was made, or treat the strictness as unratified.
findings.scenario: A PR commits `.specclaw/changes/X/review/round-N.json`. The CI template derives CHANGE=X and runs `specclaw-review verdict --change X --head <PR head>`. It exits 1 on every run, so `specclaw/review-loop` is never posted. The docs still say CI posts it.
